summary: Configured persistent name-based Apache websites on node1 TCP 8080. Both approved hostnames serve their respective preserved trees, unknown hosts receive HTTP 403, and the configuration recovered successfully after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed the CentOS-compatible Apache HTTP server.
Configured docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test as separate name-based virtual hosts sharing TCP 8080.
Configured the default virtual host to reject unknown Host headers with HTTP 403.
Added persistent firewalld and SELinux configuration.
Enabled httpd at boot without changing the CentOS release or kernel.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: docs.branch.test serves the supplied documentation tree on TCP 8080.
evidence.summary: Index and handbook requests returned HTTP 200 with the approved documentation content before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: orders.branch.test serves the supplied purchasing tree on TCP 8080.
evidence.summary: Index and catalog requests returned HTTP 200 with the approved purchasing content before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Unknown Host headers receive an error instead of tenant content.
evidence.summary: An unknown Host returned HTTP 403 and checks confirmed neither tenant's identifying content was leaked.

evidence.requirement: Both sites share TCP port 8080 with persistent service and security configuration.
evidence.summary: Apache's parsed configuration shows both named tenants and the reject-default host on *:8080; httpd is enabled and active, the listener is present, firewalld allows 8080 persistently, and SELinux remains enforcing.
SHA-256 hashes for all five staged files are identical before configuration, before restart, and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel.
evidence.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery evidence.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 5b620f5a-2111-4f37-b111-4cdf414707cf was captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to bb73add6-5dab-492f-a442-38c25552734b; and post-restart service, listener, firewall, content hashes, both websites, rejection behavior, OS, kernel, and SELinux state were verified.
